note: Voice-over for scripts/walkthrough.mjs. One entry per title() / say() call, in tour order. Abbreviations are spelled the way they should be spoken.

lines.text: This is the G-B-S Fit-Gap Workbench. It takes you from the capture sheets all the way to Q-G-2 sign-off – in one single file.
It's just one H-T-M-L file. There's nothing to install, no server, and no network connection – everything you do is saved right in your browser.
Let's load the demo data: a fictional group with three entities and all five streams, structured exactly like a real set of capture workbooks.
The start page shows the five steps, and where you are right now. The client's name and logo are picked up automatically from the workbooks.
Up here you've got the key numbers – entities, streams, activities, progress, and deviations. Always live.
Step one is planning. You set the client and the country, your initials for the audit trail, and the logo and brand colour.
Then you add the people in the room, and one session per stream. The traffic light tells you what's still missing before the workshop starts.
Step two is the workshop itself. The process tree is on the left – one row per activity, with all the entities side by side.
Each cell shows what G-B-S Operations pre-assessed. You can accept all the no-gap rows in one click, and spend your time on the ones that are actually flagged.
For every entity, it's Fit, Gap, or a question mark. Operations wasn't sure about this one – so it becomes an open question. One click.
Open a cell, and you get the full form: the activity split, F-T-E, the detailed gap fields, the gap type, the rationale, and the deviation block.
And every change is logged – with the session, the editor, and a timestamp. The audit trail is simply built in.
Here's the same process group as a flow board. There's a lane for local accounting, one for other parties, and one for G-B-S – one card per step, with the hand-offs in between.
Click a step to capture who performs it, and what's different from the global standard.
Step three is present mode. Full-screen slides for the room: a cover with the client logo, the scope, the gap types – and then one process group after another.
The flow boards stay editable while you present: who does the step today, how much capacity it takes in F-T-E, and what's different. So it's all captured live, in the meeting – no second tool.
The table slide shows the entities side by side, with the findings in each cell.
And the closing slide sums up what was assessed, the open points, and the next session.
Step four is the results. Every deviation sits on one board – with its resolution approach, the accountable owner, the escalation level, and the approval status.
Further down, you'll find the activity split against the plan, Operations versus the workshop, the change matrix, and the cross-entity view.
Step five is the Q-G-2 sign-off: readiness per entity and stream, plus the sign-off fields for the process expert and for G-B-S Operations.

The hand-over package bundles everything: the deviation log, separate variants for the D-T-Ps, initiative candidates, taxonomy change requests, the Q-G-2 summary, the flat export, and the audit trail.
And finally, the write-back puts the workshop results straight into the original capture workbooks. Values only – all the formatting stays as it is.
Capture sheets in. Decisions out. The G-B-S Fit-Gap Workbench.
